subject: eurasian wryneck
title: Reach Into This Bird's Nest and a Snake Seems to Hiss Back

scenes.text: Put your hand into this bird's nest hole, and a snake seems to be waiting.
The wryneck is a small woodpecker, barely bigger than a sparrow.
It can't fight, and its nest is a dark hole in a tree.
So when something reaches in, it twists and sways its head like a snake, and hisses.
In the dark, a predator sees a writhing neck and hears a snake. Most back off.
Its old names were snake bird and twister. The word jinx comes from it.

description:
The Eurasian wryneck, a small woodpecker that eats mostly ants, defends its nest hole by twisting its head like a snake and hissing.
In the dark of a tree hole, the act scares off predators. Its old names include snake bird and twister, and the word jinx comes from its name.
Would you put your hand back in?
thumbnail_text: THIS BIRD HISSES LIKE A SNAKE
first_comment: The bird's Latin name, Jynx, gave us the word jinx. Which animal bluff do you think works best?
